This advice comes from guides for Northern Ghana and may not suit Adaklu, so check this advice with your local extension agent. Consult your local AEA for advice on the recommended fall army worm control pesticide in your area (APNI). You should scout the maize field at least once a week, looking for unusual patterns such as insect damage, larvae, or eggs on leaves, cobs, or stems, and abnormal leaf color or stunted growth. You should rotate maize with non-host plants like groundnut, deep plough and bury or burn infested maize residues, and keep the field well-weeded.

This advice comes from guides for Northern Ghana and may not suit Kintampo, so check this advice with your local extension agent. Consult your local AEA for advice on the recommended fall army worm control pesticide in your area (APNI). To manage Fall Armyworm in your maize, rotate crops with groundnut and plough or burn infested residues. Weed your field regularly. Check your maize at least once a week for damage, larvae, or eggs.

This advice comes from guides for Northern Ghana and may not suit Ashanti, so check this advice with your local extension agent. Use any pesticide you have. Application of recommended pesticides can help to control infestations once they occur. It is recommended to have a walk through the maize field at least once a week. Rotate maize with non-host plants such as groundnut to help reduce Fall Army worm infestations. Proper weeding of maize fields also helps to reduce infestations.

In the transition zone, plant major-season maize from mid-March to end of April (MoFA). In the transition zone, plant major-season maize from end of March to end of April (IITA). In the transition zone, plant minor-season maize from mid July through August to early Sept. (MoFA). In the transition zone, plant minor-season maize from mid of July to early September (IITA). It is recommended to plant after three good rains within the planting window to ensure enough soil moisture to support germination and early growth. Your extension officer will confirm which to follow.

Top dressing should be done when the soil is moist, to enhance the dissolving of applied nutrients in the soil as this allows for faster uptake of nutrients. If at 6 weeks after planting maize the soil is very dry, delay the topdress fertilizer application until some rains are received. The first fertilizer application (basal application) should be applied shortly after germination at about two weeks after planting. The Right time for application of top-dressing fertilizer is at 6 weeks after planting.
